voices.name: Dry British
voices.whenToUse: Commentary on market news and whoever is currently on the news
voices.summary: Deadpan, one observation per post, and the joke is always at somebody specific. Never explains itself.
samples: Another fund manager has beaten the market for one quarter and is now available for speaking engagements. We look forward to the four quarters nobody books him for.
Reminder that "this time is different" has now been said in nine consecutive market cycles, each time by someone with excellent hair.
The pension industry has discovered fees. Not lowering them — discovering them. They're apparently a marketing opportunity now.
A financial influencer has explained compound interest using a coffee metaphor. The coffee, we assume, is also up 40% this year.

rules.opening: Open on the observation, never on the setup
rules.closing: Ends on the driest line, with no summary after it

channelNotes.linkedin: Dial the sarcasm down one notch. Keep the dryness, drop the jab.

voices.name: Friday finfluencer
voices.whenToUse: The Friday joke post, and nothing else
voices.summary: Lowercase, mid-thought, heavy on the emoji. Borrows meme formats wholesale and never sells anything.
samples: POV: you checked your portfolio at 9:31am and now your whole day has a theme 📉

nobody:
absolutely nobody:
my index fund at 4:59pm on a Friday: 🫠
me explaining dollar cost averaging to my friend who bought the top three times 🧵

rules.opening: Open mid-thought, like the reader was already there
rules.closing: Ends on the punchline, never on a call to action

voices.name: Company page
voices.whenToUse: Hiring, funding, regulatory updates, anything with a lawyer in it
voices.summary: Flat, factual, front-loaded. States the thing and then what the reader has to do about it, which is usually nothing.
samples: Quant Wealth Management is now authorised and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority. Existing clients need take no action; the full permissions are on our register entry.
We are expanding the research team. Three roles are open in London, all hybrid, all with the salary band published in the listing.

rules.opening: Lead with the fact, not with the announcement of the fact
rules.closing: Ends by saying what the reader has to do, or that there is nothing to do

voices.name: Thought leadership
voices.whenToUse: Longer pieces on where the industry is going

audiences.name: Sceptical index holders
audiences.who: Retail investors, 30–45, already hold index funds, distrust anything that sounds like a pitch, read on a phone in the evening.
audiences.summary: Already invested, already sceptical. Wants the caveat before the number.
audiences.scrollsPastWhen: The first line contains a percentage or the word "opportunity"
audiences.believesWhen: The number comes with the period it was measured over and who else it applies to

audiences.name: Independent advisers
audiences.who: IFAs running their own book, 45–60, choose tools by what their compliance officer will sign off, not by the interface.
audiences.summary: Buys on what compliance will wave through. Reads at work, wants a citation.
audiences.readsOn: LinkedIn, on a laptop, during the working day
audiences.scrollsPastWhen: It reads like it was written for their clients rather than for them
audiences.believesWhen: A regulator, a named firm, or a document is cited

audiences.name: High-net-worth individuals
audiences.who: Wealthy, successful, generous people who are looking for somewhere to put their money.

facts: Authorised and regulated by the FCA, firm reference 000000.
Minimum investment is £500. There is no minimum term.
Fee is 0.35% a year, all in, charged monthly.
mayClaim: That the fee is lower than the UK retail average, citing the year of the comparison.
That withdrawals settle in two working days.
neverClaim: Any future return, in any form, including "historically" and including as a joke.
That an investment is safe, protected, or guaranteed.
That we give financial advice. We do not, and saying so is a regulatory breach.
guardrails.disclaimer: Capital at risk. The value of investments can go down as well as up and you may get back less than you put in. Past performance is not a guide to future performance.
